discovery: Invention and development of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock, trapping neutral atoms at a 'magic wavelength' so that the lattice light shifts both clock levels equally, letting thousands of atoms be interrogated at once without perturbing the transition. He and Ye turned this idea into working instruments, and Ye's group pushed systematic uncertainties and stability to the 10^-18 level and below, with coherent many-atom spectroscopy. These clocks now outperform the caesium standard by over two orders of magnitude and will drive the redefinition of the SI second. Just as important for fundamental physics, they resolve the gravitational redshift over millimetre heights, constrain variations of fundamental constants, and search for ultralight dark matter, making them one of the sharpest quantum sensors for physics beyond the Standard Model. This is a clear case of deep insight combined with outstanding engineering that has opened new routes to old questions.
